findings.title: nil map panic on quota increment
findings.description: NewStore never initializes the quota map, so every Create call writes to a nil map and panics.

findings.title: expired-link check is inverted
findings.description: Resolve deletes links whose expiry is still in the future and keeps expired ones, the opposite of intended behavior.

findings.title: Metrics.AddResolved uses value receiver
findings.description: AddResolved locks a copy of the mutex, so concurrent calls race on the shared counters.

findings.title: evict deadlocks by calling Get under write lock
findings.description: evict holds c.mu and calls c.Get, which tries to acquire the read lock; sync.RWMutex is not reentrant.

findings.title: mutating cache under read lock
findings.description: Get deletes expired entries and updates used/hits while holding only an RLock.

findings.title: sessions map accessed without synchronization
findings.description: Issue, Verify, Revoke and Middleware touch the shared sessions map concurrently.

findings.title: admin endpoint trusts X-Admin header
findings.description: adminQuotas checks a client-supplied header instead of the authenticated session role, allowing anyone to read quotas.

findings.title: delete endpoint skips ownership check
findings.description: deleteLink removes any link without verifying the caller owns it.

findings.title: BearerToken panics on malformed header
findings.description: parts[1] is accessed without length check, causing index-out-of-range on bad Authorization headers.

findings.title: RequireAdmin always rejects
findings.description: The condition uses OR, making it always true, so valid admins are always denied.

findings.title: token leaked in 401 response body
findings.description: The unauthorized error message echoes the supplied token, aiding token theft.

findings.title: division by zero when no links
findings.description: stats computes hits / len(links) without guarding empty link set.

findings.title: Page slice end off by one
findings.description: end can be len(all)+1, which panics on all[offset:end].

findings.title: WaitGroup.Add called inside goroutine
findings.description: WarmCache launches goroutines before Add, racing Wait and losing synchronization.

findings.title: CheckTargets leaks goroutines and can panic
findings.description: Unbuffered results channel blocks abandoned goroutines; mustHead returns nil on error causing client.Do panic.

findings.title: Rename validates from twice
findings.description: The to code is never validated before being used as a key.

findings.title: SuccessRate integer division truncates to zero
findings.description: used / len * 100 evaluates division first, yielding 0 for any partial usage.

findings.title: Top sorts ascending
findings.description: The leaderboard returns least-followed links first, contrary to its contract.

findings.title: export file mode too permissive
findings.description: WriteFile uses 0666 although the report is meant to be owner-only.

findings.title: open redirect in /out
findings.description: next query value is used directly in a redirect, enabling phishing redirects.

findings.title: SSRF via preview fetch
findings.description: preview fetches an arbitrary stored target, including internal addresses.

findings.title: cache TTL uses seconds instead of milliseconds
findings.description: LINKD_CACHE_TTL_MS is documented as milliseconds but multiplied by time.Second.

findings.title: Validate never returns an error
findings.description: Validate always returns nil even when problems are found, so bad configs start the server.

findings.title: Import is not atomic
findings.description: Links are written one by one; a validation failure midway leaves partial state.

findings.title: Quotas returns internal map
findings.description: Callers can mutate the store's quota map because the same reference is returned.

findings.title: Store has no concurrency protection
findings.description: Store methods mutate maps without locks while HTTP handlers and janitor use them concurrently.

findings.title: ByOwner uses substring match
findings.description: strings.Contains may return links owned by a different but similarly named owner.

findings.title: Extend revives expired links
findings.description: Extend always pushes expiry into the future, contradicting the documented permanent expiry.

findings.title: Store has no synchronization for concurrent map access
findings.description: Store.links and Store.quota are plain maps mutated by every handler (Create, Resolve, Delete, Rename, Import, Prune, …) while the janitor goroutine launched in worker.StartJanitor iterates and deletes from s.links directly. HTTP handlers run concurrently and the janitor ticks every minute, so any interleaving is a data race (and Go map concurrent read/write is fatal). StartJanitor's direct map access makes the unsafety worse.

findings.title: Authenticator.sessions map accessed without synchronization
findings.description: Issue writes to sessions, Verify ranges over it, and Revoke deletes from it, with no mutex. Woven into HTTP serving via Middleware, these run concurrently, risking a data race and concurrent-map-iteration/write panics.

findings.title: Cache is documented thread-safe but is not
findings.description: Get mutates e.used and c.hits while holding only an RLock and deletes from c.m under RLock; Peek, Warm, and Stats touch maps/fields with no lock at all; Warm calls Set (which locks) in a loop without any overall synchronization. Any concurrent use races and can corrupt state or panic.

findings.title: Deadlocks in Cache: evict calls Get while holding write lock; Delete fails to unlock on early return
findings.description: evict holds c.mu and calls c.Get, which tries to acquire RLock on the same RWMutex, blocking forever. Delete returns early when the code is absent without calling Unlock, leaving the lock held forever. Timer callbacks also call Delete, so a firing timer can deadlock against any holder.

findings.title: Metrics.AddResolved uses a value receiver, copying the mutex
findings.description: AddResolved is declared func (m Metrics) with a value receiver while the other methods use *Metrics. Each call locks a private copy of sync.Mutex and increments a field on a thrown-away copy, so the resolved counter stays zero and the lock provides no real protection. Store? no. This is visible on every redirect path.

findings.title: WarmCache calls wg.Add inside the goroutine
findings.description: wg.Add(1) is executed by the spawned goroutine instead of before starting it, so wg.Wait() can return before any goroutine increments the counter (or a counter becomes negative). This is a data race on the WaitGroup and defeats the 'returns after every probe finished' contract.

findings.title: CheckTargets leaks goroutines on early error
findings.description: Goroutines send their result on an unbuffered channel. When the receive loop returns on the first error (line ~100-102), the remaining goroutines block forever on `results <-`, leaking. With many links this accumulates goroutines per request.

findings.title: Janitor sweeps store maps directly without synchronization
findings.description: StartJanitor iterates s.links and deletes entries outside of any Store method and without locking. Even if Store gains a mutex, this bypasses it, racing with handlers.

findings.title: preview does not close resp.Body
findings.description: The http.Response body is read but never closed, leaking connections/file descriptors under concurrent load; combined with the shared client this degrades the process.

findings.title: Admin endpoint trusts client-supplied X-Admin header
findings.description: adminQuotas checks r.Header.Get("X-Admin") == "true" and the middleware never sets that header, so any caller can mint admin access by sending X-Admin: true and read every owner's link counts. This is an authorization bypass.

findings.title: Path traversal in export filename
findings.description: ExportCSV joins dir with name+".csv" without sanitizing name, so values like ../../etc/foo traverse outside the export directory and can overwrite arbitrary files with a .csv suffix.

findings.title: SSRF via preview endpoint
findings.description: preview resolves a stored link and calls s.client.Get(target) with no host allowlist, then returns the response body. An attacker can store a link to an internal address (e.g. 169.254.169.254) and exfiltrate internal responses through /preview.

findings.title: Session tokens generated with math/rand
findings.description: Issue builds tokens from math/rand.Intn, whose output is predictable and not cryptographically secure, making issued session tokens guessable.

findings.title: Issued session token written to logs
findings.description: log.Printf prints the full token, leaking live credentials in log files.

findings.title: Token echoed back in 401 response
findings.description: The unauthorized error message includes the supplied token, disclosing a credential to anyone probing the API.

findings.title: Session expiry never enforced
findings.description: Verify performs no ExpiresAt check, so issued tokens remain valid forever, defeating the 12-hour lifetime and revocation expectations.

findings.title: Hardcoded fallback secret
findings.description: NewAuthenticator falls back to "dev-secret-do-not-use" when LINKD_SECRET is unset, allowing a known secret in any deployment that omits the env var.

findings.title: deleteLink performs no ownership check
findings.description: Despite its comment, Delete is called with only the code; any authenticated user can delete any link, an IDOR/authorization gap.

findings.title: Open redirect via ?next=
findings.description: out redirects to an arbitrary, unvalidated next URL, enabling phishing through a trusted host.

findings.title: BearerToken panics on malformed Authorization header
findings.description: parts[1] is accessed without checking the split length, so a malformed header causes an index-out-of-range panic and denial of service.

findings.title: Password hashing uses unsalted SHA-256
findings.description: HashPassword is a single SHA-256 digest with no salt, leaving stored passwords vulnerable to rainbow-table and precomputation attacks.

findings.title: Export file created world-readable/writable
findings.description: os.WriteFile uses mode 0666, contradicting the code's own intent that only the service user read the report and exposing all owners' link data.

findings.title: Wildcard CORS combined with credentials
findings.description: writeJSON sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * alongside Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, an insecure configuration that can enable cross-origin credential use.

findings.title: ByOwner matches owner by substring
findings.description: strings.Contains(l.Owner, owner) returns links for any owner containing the query, leaking other owners' data when an owner value is a substring of another.

findings.title: RequireAdmin condition is always true
findings.description: The check `s.Role != "admin" || s.Role != "owner"` is true for every role, so the gate rejects everyone and any caller relying on it can never be an admin as intended; combined with the X-Admin header path this leaves admin access to header forgery.

findings.title: WarmCache/CheckTargets issue requests to user-controlled targets
findings.description: These helpers perform outbound HTTP HEAD requests to link targets without host validation, allowing internal-network probing if invoked with attacker-controlled links.
